snip.t: Most in adult life with CKD(stage 3), hypertension and small kidneys.\nelectrolyte abnormalities are typically more severe, resulting in hyperkalaemia and acidosis(tubular unresponsiveness)
| Renal Ultrasound | Kidney size, structure, hydronephrosis, cysts | Small kidneys (CKD), hydronephrosis (obstruction) |
| Chronic kidney disease (stage 5) | Long‑standing hypertension, proteinuria, small kidneys on US | Dialysis indicated when uremic/volume/electrolyte criteria met |
| Renal ultrasound | Size, obstruction, echogenicity | Small kidneys = chronic disease; hydronephrosis = obstructive cause |
Abdominal ultrasound: Ascites, liver size, renal size — Small kidneys = chronic disease; large liver with nodularity = cirrhosis
| Tubulointerstitial disease from TB or HIV | History of TB, low-grade fever, sterile pyuria | Imaging shows small kidneys, urine eosinophils absent, PCR for TB or HIV viral load positive |
CKD with acute on chronic; differentiate by chronic stigmata (small kidneys on US, persistent proteinuria).
